newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan to privatise state airline next year.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan to privatise state airline next year.

text.p: Pakistan plans to sell chunks of its state-owned telecom utility, airline, railways and banks as part of anaccelerated New Year privatisation drive.

Salman Shah, chairman of the state Privatisation Commission, told Reuters in an interview on Tuesday that a team from the International Finance Corporation (IFC) was preparing a proposal for privatisation of Pakistan International Airlines (PIA).
"The IFC people have visited the head office of the PIA and now we expect to get some proposals from them which should be ready in the next couple of days," Shah said.
"Basically what we are looking for is a major alliance partner for PIA which can contribute towards its equity and take over its management," Shah added.
Shah said that if everything went smoothly, PIA would have a strategic partner within six to nine months. "I think that is a sufficient time period," he added.
Work had also begun on phased privatisation of Pakistan Railways. "We are taking a summary to the cabinet for railways which we are going to move towards privatisation," he said.
In the preparatory phase, Pakistan Railways would be restructured by dividing it into three or four commercial units.

"The idea is to make it a commercially-oriented organisation which can serve the need of consumers," he said. "Once we have restructured the railways, we will let them compete with road and air transport.

"Inshallah (God willing) we will put the framework in place in the next month or so, then different phases will take their own time. I assume that we should be able to privatise railways in the next 12 to 16 months," Shah said.

Pakistan's plans to sell a 26 percent stake and transfer the management of the Pakistan Telecommunication Company Ltd (PTCL) have been hanging fire since December 1995, but Shah said the project had not been shelved or put off.
